🔴 RENOVATE CANNOT REGENERATE `pubspec.lock` FOR THIS PIN, AND IT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT CONFIG.
This version is matched by a regex customManager in renovate.json against THIS file. Renovate
dispatches artifact updates BY MANAGER ID, and lib/modules/manager/custom/regex exports only
`extractPackageFile` — no `updateArtifacts`. So a branch from that rule carries ZERO artifact
updates by construction — and THAT half is the one that settles it, because it holds whoever runs
Renovate.
⚠️ THE SECOND HALF OF THIS PARAGRAPH CHANGED ON 2026-09-03 AND IS CORRECTED RATHER THAN DELETED.
It read 'this repo is on the HOSTED Mend app, where `postUpgradeTasks` runs against an allow-list

to set (RENOVATE_ALLOWED_POST_UPGRADE_COMMANDS). The vendor objection is therefore gone; the
structural one above is not, and it is sufficient on its own: a regex customManager emits no
artifact updates for any host. ⛔ Still do not file 'teach Renovate to do it' as the fix — but if
anyone reopens it, the thing to attack is the MANAGER, never the host. Researched 2026-08-28;
re-checked against the self-hosted move 2026-09-03.
SO EVERY BUMP OF THIS PIN NEEDS A HUMAN (or a dispatch job) WITH THE NEW SDK, TO:
1. `flutter pub get` at the repo root ON THE NEW SDK, and commit the regenerated pubspec.lock.
⛔ NEVER on the OLD SDK — that writes the OLD pins back. 3.44.9 -> 3.47.1 moved SEVEN
SDK-constrained packages (intl, matcher, meta, test, test_api, test_core, vector_math) and
`--enforce-lockfile` is invoked at THIRTEEN call sites. Only ci.yml runs on pull_request;
the other twelve fire on merge, on tag, on the nightly and on every store submission — so a

2. Re-stamp the brick and run both format gates. ⚠️ Stamped apps are language version 3.9 since

resolved stamp formats under the same language version as the unresolved CI gate; at the old

⚠️ AND ONE THING 3.47 DOES THAT YOU MUST NOT COMMIT. Under 3.47.1 EVERY `flutter pub get` —
including `--enforce-lockfile` — rewrites `analysis_options.yaml`, appending an `analyzer:

suppressing a rule, and invisible in every report that counts rules"). Revert those seven files
after any local pub get. It is safe in CI only because the guard runs in the `platform` job while
every pub get runs in `app_brick` / `workspace_gate` — different runners, fresh checkouts. If a
pub get is ever added to the `platform` job, that job goes red and this paragraph is why.

$xcode_comment: THE APPLE TOOLCHAIN FLOOR — AND IT IS A STORE POLICY, NOT A PACKAGE VERSION.
developer.apple.com/news/upcoming-requirements/ (fetched 2026-07-29, recorded in
Private/requirements/ — was pipeline/10-distribution-store.md, folded into the JSON spec 2026-08-15): apps uploaded to App Store Connect 'must be built
with Xcode 26 or later' — effective 28 April 2026, so it is ALREADY IN FORCE, not upcoming.
WHY IT IS DECLARED HERE WHILE NO LANE READS IT YET. tooling/channel-register.json's
`minimumToolchain` names versions.json KEYS, never values ([pipeline F-2]) — so until this key
existed the ios-appstore and macos-appstore rows named a floor that resolved to nothing, and
assert-channel-register.mjs printed `(deferred) needs a pinned \`xcode\`` on every run. That
print was CORRECT and it is what this line closes. The register's ios-appstore `notes` recorded
the same gap in prose ('tooling/versions.json has no `xcode` key') and was corrected in the same
change — a note that outlives the gap it describes is the defect this repo keeps paying for.
⚠️ THIS IS NOT THE XCODE CI RUNS, AND NOTHING HERE CLAIMS IT IS. build-platforms.yml pins the
runner IMAGE (`runner_macos`) and the image decides which Xcode is selected; $runners_comment
below records windows-2025 changing COMPILERS under an unchanged pin, which is the identical
hazard one platform over. Selecting an Xcode in the Apple lane (`xcode-select -s`, or
maxim-lobanov/setup-xcode) is deferred with the Apple channels themselves (unsigned; OWNER_QUEUE A-4 closed 2026-08-31), so
tooling/ci/assert-version-consistency.mjs carries NO rule for this key and compares it to no
call site. That is a STATED GAP rather than an oversight: a drift rule whose scan has no target
is an assertion that cannot fail, and this repository deletes those instead of counting them.
🔴 THE VALUE IS A FLOOR, SO IT IS A MAJOR AND NOT A FULL VERSION. Apple's sentence is 'Xcode 26
or later'. Writing 26.6 would pin whatever Xcode the macos-26 image happened to carry on the day
somebody looked (the ios-appstore row's own notes record 'Xcode 26.6 / 17F113'), and a floor
that moves with the image is not a floor — it is the image, restated. Same shape as `node`
and `java` above, which are majors for the same reason.
$runners_comment: PINNED — owner decision 2026-07-26. Previously all 17 `runs-on:` values were
'-latest', which carries the same hazard as a floating action tag: macos-latest
rolling to a new Xcode changes what an identical commit builds, with no diff in
the repo at all.
Why pinning helps here: '-latest' rolls to a whole new OS image unannounced in
your repo, while a pinned label at least fails loudly when the image is finally
retired. That is the same principle every other guard in tooling/ci serves.
🔴 CORRECTED 2026-07-28 — this used to claim a pinned image 'fails LOUDLY and ON
A SCHEDULE' while '-latest' fails 'SILENTLY and UNSCHEDULED'. That overstates it,
and GitHub's own changelog is the counter-example:
https://github.blog/changelog/2026-05-14-github-actions-upcoming-image-migrations/
'The `windows-latest` AND `windows-2025` labels in GitHub Actions will be
migrated to use Visual Studio 2026 by default.'  (rolled out 8-15 June 2026;
`windows-2022` is the way to stay on VS 2022.)
So our Windows lane changed COMPILERS under an unchanged pin, silently, with no
diff in this repo — exactly the failure the original wording promised pinning
prevented. PINNING A RUNNER LABEL NARROWS THE DRIFT; IT DOES NOT REMOVE IT.
A label names an image family, not an immutable image.
Kept anyway: narrower drift is still worth having, and the alternative ('-latest')
drifts across OS major versions rather than tool versions. But do not read these
pins as a guarantee of a reproducible toolchain — they are not one.
Cost, stated plainly: images are eventually retired and CI then breaks hard
rather than drifting. These land in the SAME maintenance bucket as the F-11
action pins, so one mechanism — Renovate, stage 14 — covers both.
Labels verified against actions/runner-images README before pinning, not
guessed: a wrong label yields 'no runner matching the labels' and the job never
starts. Current aliases: ubuntu-latest→24.04, windows-latest→2025, macos-latest
→macOS 26 Arm64.
$wrangler_comment: ADDED 2026-07-28 after the external-facts pass found the worst kind of drift:
the tool that PUBLISHES production was not on this list at all.
cloudflare/wrangler-action runs `npm i wrangler@<version>`. It resolves that
version from the package.json in `workingDirectory` — and deploy-web.yml points
it at `apps/subscriptiontracker`, which is a Flutter app with NO package.json. So the action
fell back to the constant compiled into its own bundle: 3.90.0.
Live-proven, not inferred: run 30292045671 (2026-07-27) logs
`npm i wrangler@3.90.0` while both Workers lock 4.114.0. A MAJOR version behind
the rest of the repo, past its bug-fix window per Cloudflare's own changelog,
holding the account API token, and chosen by a third party's default.
F-2 says every version is declared once and F-11 says build inputs are pinned.
Both read VERIFIED while this was true, because both looked at what the repo
WRITES and never at what the deploy RESOLVES.
4.114.0 -> 4.120.0 on 2026-08-10, and the REASON matters more than the number:
wrangler <= 4.119.0 depends on a miniflare that depends on undici < 7.29.0, which
carries six advisories including a cross-user cache-disclosure high (alerts 16-27).
4.120.0 is the FIRST fixed release, so there was no smaller move available.
⚠️ WHAT THIS BUYS THE BRICK, AND WHAT IT COSTS IT. wrangler 4.120.0 depends on
`miniflare@5.20260801.1-alpha` — an ALPHA, where 4.114.0 depended on the stable
`miniflare@4.20260722.0`. The two committed Worker lockfiles are immune to that:
they pin the resolved tree, so an unpublish cannot reach them. THE STAMPED SERVICE
IS NOT — it has no lockfile by construction and `npm install`s fresh every run,
which is exactly how `^4.0.0` floated onto 4.117.0 and died with `notarget` on an
alpha miniflare that had gone away (see assert-version-consistency.mjs:76-90).
Verified before landing, not assumed: a from-scratch `npm install` of the brick's
exact declaration set resolves wrangler 4.120.0 + miniflare 5.20260801.1-alpha and
exits 0 today. If a stamp ever fails with `notarget` on miniflare, THIS is the line
to read first, and the fix is to move this pin forward to a wrangler whose miniflare
is published — never to reintroduce the caret.
4.120.0 -> 4.129.0 on 2026-09-07 (Renovate PR #535). The paragraph above stands as
written about 4.120.0; what follows supersedes only the version numbers in it.
4.129.0 carries `miniflare@5.20260903.0-alpha` (still an alpha, still published
today) and `workerd@1.20260903.1`. The brick check the paragraph above demands was
re-run rather than inherited: a from-scratch `npm install --package-lock-only` of
the brick's exact declaration set resolves wrangler 4.129.0 + miniflare
5.20260903.0-alpha + @cloudflare/workers-types 5.20260907.1 and exits 0.
🔴 NEW WITH THIS BUMP, AND IT IS WHY TWO LOCKFILES MOVED THAT NOTHING NAMED:
wrangler 4.129.0 declares `peerOptional @cloudflare/workers-types@^5.20260903.1`,
which the committed 5.20260810.1 does NOT satisfy. npm refuses outright —
`ERESOLVE could not resolve ... Conflicting peer dependency` — so the two Worker
lockfiles could not take wrangler alone; each moved 9 packages / 36 lines (wrangler,
miniflare, workerd + its 5 platform binaries, and workers-types). That move is NOT
caret drift to be frozen out: it is a line the bump MAKES, and freezing it is what
produces the ERESOLVE. The stamped service is unaffected — its
`@cloudflare/workers-types: ^5.20260714.1` already admits the peer, verified above.
assert-version-consistency.mjs does not read either lockfile, so nothing would have
told you: `npm ci` in services/*/ is the check, and it exits 0 on both.
$glitchtip_cli_comment: ADDED 2026-09-03. THE TOOL THAT MAKES A WEB CRASH READABLE, and until this key existed there was
no such tool in the tree at all.
MEASURED, not suspected: GET /api/0/organizations/nikatru/releases/{version}/files/ answers 200
with a ZERO-LENGTH list for every one of the 12 releases GlitchTip holds for project `subscriptiontracker`, and
`dsyms` is []. Nothing has ever been uploaded. The consequence is two OPEN, UNRESOLVED production
issues nobody can read: `minified:a0X: GoError: There is nothing to pop` (4 occurrences, level
fatal) and `minified:ng: AuthException(...)`, whose frames read `main.dart.js k7.er 63099`.
🔴 glitchtip-cli, NOT sentry-cli, AND THE CHOICE IS THE WHOLE POINT. sentry-cli against a
self-hosted GlitchTip has standing reports of EXITING 0 WHILE STORING NOTHING (glitchtip#38,
glitchtip-backend#299) — the one failure shape this repository refuses everywhere else, because a
green step that uploaded nothing is indistinguishable from a green step that worked until six
weeks later when a crash needs reading. glitchtip-cli is the vendor's own client for the vendor's
own server.
⚠️ THE DIGEST BELOW IS PART OF THIS PIN, NOT A SEPARATE FACT. A version number names a release;
the sha256 names the BYTES. The release asset is served from a GitLab job artifact
(/-/jobs/artifacts/v<ver>/raw/...), which is a mutable-by-construction address in a way a git tag
is not — re-running that job would republish under the same URL. Same reasoning as F-11's
40-character action SHAs: a label is not an address. Renovate can move `glitchtip_cli`; it cannot
compute the digest, so a bump PR arrives RED at the checksum step until a human supplies the new
one. That is deliberate and it is loud — the alternative is a bump that silently installs bytes
nobody has looked at, holding a GlitchTip auth token.
VERIFIED 2026-09-03 BY RUNNING THE BINARY, not by reading the docs page: v1.0.0 is
`glitchtip-cli 1.0.0`, a 14,420,352-byte static-pie ELF; `sourcemaps upload` takes
-r/--release, -d/--dist, -u/--url-prefix (default `~`), -o/--org, -p/--project and --validate,
and it DISCOVERS .js/.map pairs WITHOUT debug IDs (`Found 2 file(s) to upload.` on a fixture that
had none), so `sourcemaps inject` is not a precondition. It reads SENTRY_URL, SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN
and SENTRY_ORG from the environment — also proven by running it, because `releases new --url`
SHADOWS the global `--url` with 'Optional URL for this release', so passing the server address as
a flag there would post the release to sentry.io. deploy-web.yml therefore passes the server
address ONLY as SENTRY_URL.
$glitchtip_cli_platform_digests_comment: ADDED 2026-09-07, unit `symbols-everywhere` ([ADR 067] decision 6, programme.json P1-11). THE
REASON ELEVEN OF FOURTEEN RELEASE BUILDS UPLOADED NOTHING, WRITTEN DOWN IN FOUR PLACES, WAS
'tooling/versions.json pins ONE glitchtip-cli and it is linux-x86_64'. That sentence was TRUE and
it excused SEVEN lanes (windows x3, macOS x2, iOS x2) — never the other four, which run on
ubuntu-24.04 where the pinned Linux binary already works. Those four are wired without touching
this block at all; these two keys are what the remaining seven needed.
🔴 THERE IS ONE VERSION AND THREE SETS OF BYTES. `glitchtip_cli` above names the release and is
the ONLY key Renovate advances; these two are digests of the OTHER TWO ARTIFACTS OF THAT SAME
RELEASE, exactly as `glitchtip_cli_sha256` is the digest of the linux one. Adding a second
VERSION key would be the drift this whole file exists to refuse — three pins that can disagree
about which glitchtip-cli the pipeline speaks.
THE ASSET NAMES ARE READ FROM THE PROJECT'S OWN .gitlab-ci.yml AT TAG v1.0.0, not guessed:
`release:` declares four asset links, and the job that builds each is the `?job=` query the URL
needs — build-linux-x86_64 -> glitchtip-cli-linux-x86_64, build-windows-x86_64 ->
glitchtip-cli-windows-x86_64.exe, build-macos-arm64 -> glitchtip-cli-macos-arm64
(aarch64-apple-darwin, which is what the macos-26 runner is; an x86_64 runner would fail CLOSED
at the `--version` check the install step already makes, never silently).
MEASURED 2026-09-07 BY DOWNLOADING ALL THREE AND HASHING THEM, in one pass, with the LINUX one
included as the control: it re-derived `de1c035a…82dfef` byte for byte, which is what makes the
two new digests evidence rather than assertion. Sizes, for the record, since a digest alone
cannot tell you a truncated download from a different build: linux 14,420,352 bytes; windows
22,165,194 bytes; macOS 12,055,312 bytes.
⚠️ SAME MECHANISM, SAME DELIBERATE RED as the linux digest: a GitLab JOB ARTIFACT URL is a
re-runnable address rather than an immutable object, Renovate cannot compute a checksum, so a
bump of `glitchtip_cli` lands RED at each lane's checksum step until a human downloads the three
new assets and writes all three digests here. ⛔ Do NOT 'fix' that red by deleting a checksum
step — it is the only thing standing between a bump and unlooked-at bytes holding a GlitchTip
auth token.
$scanners_comment: THE FOUR SECURITY SCANNERS, MOVED HERE 2026-09-06 ([ADR 067] decision 4, phase 2 unit
ci-security-lanes). Until this block existed all four were written as `env:` literals inside the
`security-scan` job of .github/workflows/ci.yml and NOWHERE ELSE, which is three separate
defects wearing one shape:
1. THEY WERE OUTSIDE F-2. tooling/versions.json is 'THE SINGLE DECLARATION of every version the
build depends on', and four of them were not in it. Nothing was drifting yet only because
each literal happened to be written exactly once — a property of today's file, not a
mechanism, and the identical state `wrangler` was in until 2026-08-02.
2. THEY WERE OUTSIDE THE UPDATE MECHANISM. [pipeline 14]O-9 says every pinned input is advanced
by something on a cadence or carries a written exemption, and
tooling/ci/assert-update-coverage.mjs enforces exactly that — over the keys IN THIS FILE. A
pin in a workflow's `env:` block is invisible to it, so these four were advanced by nobody
and no guard could say so. That is strictly worse than not pinning them, and it is the
sentence assert-update-coverage.mjs already prints about any key it cannot reach. Each now
has a `customManagers` entry in renovate.json against the `github-releases` datasource.
3. THE SCANNERS ARE THE LANE THAT FINDS EVERYTHING ELSE. A stale gitleaks does not go red — it
goes QUIET, which is this repository's most-recorded failure shape. OSV-Scanner is also the
only scanner in the stack that reads pubspec.lock, and Play Console blocks updates on
vulnerable SDK versions, so its currency has a store consequence.
⚠️ EACH VERSION CARRIES ITS OWN sha256, AND THE DIGEST IS PART OF THE PIN. Same reasoning as
$glitchtip_cli_comment: a version names a release, the digest names the BYTES. ci.yml reads both
halves at run time with `node -p` — the idiom deploy-web.yml already uses for glitchtip_cli and
wrangler — so no literal is left in a WORKFLOW to drift.
🔴 CORRECTED 2026-09-06, SAME DAY, BY MEASUREMENT. The sentence that stood here claimed there was
no literal left anywhere and that assert-version-consistency.mjs 'correctly carries no rule for
these keys: a drift rule whose scan has no target is an assertion that cannot fail'. A target
exists and `git grep -n VALIDATED_AGAINST` finds it: tooling/ci/scan-secrets.mjs declares
`const VALIDATED_AGAINST = '8.30.1'`, the gitleaks release its `scanned ~N bytes` volume parser
was measured against, and that constant is a SECOND LIVE COPY of the `gitleaks` value below. On
main the two could only move by the same hand, because no update mechanism reached either. This
change gives `gitleaks` a Renovate customManager, so a BOT now moves one copy — which is what
turned a dormant duplicate into a drift that could happen by itself. Mutation-proven before the
rule existed: bumping `gitleaks` here to 8.31.0 left assert-version-consistency AND
assert-update-coverage both at exit 0, and every other guard whose subject includes this file
was run and none of them bit either.
➡️ assert-version-consistency.mjs now carries a `gitleaks (scan-secrets VALIDATED_AGAINST)` rule,
scan-secrets.mjs is a REQUIRED target of that scan, and a per-file REQUIRED_YIELD entry catches
the constant being rewritten past the regex instead of drifting. ⛔ DO NOT 'fix' a red bump by
pointing VALIDATED_AGAINST at this file: scan-secrets.mjs compares the INSTALLED gitleaks against

scanner keys genuinely have no second literal, and that is a MEASUREMENT rather than the
assumption the deleted sentence made. Re-derive it with one command, which returned nothing on

git grep -nE '(zizmor|osv[-_]scanner|trivy|trufflehog)[^0-9]{0,40}[0-9]+[.][0-9]+[.][0-9]+'
⚠️ A bare `git grep` for the VALUES is not the check and must not be substituted for it: 2.5.1
and 1.28.0 match Apple guideline numbers and unrelated fixture text all over this tree, so the
search has to be anchored on the tool's NAME. That is the shape of the mistake this correction
exists to record.
🔴 SO A RENOVATE BUMP OF ANY OF THESE FOUR ARRIVES RED at ci.yml's `sha256sum -c` step until a
human downloads the new asset and writes its digest here. That failure IS the mechanism, not a
gap in it — exactly as recorded for glitchtip_cli. ⛔ Do NOT 'fix' a red bump by deleting a
checksum step.
⚠️ AND THE ASSET NAMES ARE NOT UNIFORM, which is why ci.yml still spells each URL out rather
than templating one. gitleaks ships `gitleaks_<ver>_linux_x64.tar.gz` (the version appears TWICE
and there is no leading `v` inside the filename); zizmor ships a target-triple name

A single templated URL would have to invent three of those four and would break silently on the
next vendor whose naming differs.
$trufflehog_comment: 🔴 THIS PIN IS THE SCANNER, NOT THE ACTION, AND THE TWO ARE DIFFERENT SUPPLY CHAINS.
.github/workflows/trufflehog.yml pins `trufflesecurity/trufflehog` by commit SHA. That SHA pins
the WRAPPER: a composite action whose only real step is
`docker run --rm -v .:/tmp -w /tmp "${IMAGE}:${VERSION}" git file:///tmp/ ... --fail --no-update`.
Its `version` input DEFAULTS TO "latest" (read from action.yml at the pinned commit
363923b901c911a9164f50b6c423f47c15372b1c on 2026-09-06), so a workflow that passes only `path`
and `extra_args` runs ghcr.io/trufflesecurity/trufflehog:latest — a floating tag resolved fresh
from a third-party registry on every run, outside F-2's single declaration and outside
[pipeline 14]O-9's update coverage. That was the state the first version of this lane shipped in,
and it was the exact defect the four keys above were moved out of ci.yml to fix, reintroduced one
workflow over by the same commit. The workflow now reads this key with `node -p` and passes it as
`version:`.
⚠️ THE TAG CARRIES NO LEADING `v` AND THE GIT TAG DOES. Measured against the registry on
2026-09-06: ghcr.io/trufflesecurity/trufflehog publishes `3.97.4` and has no `v3.97.4` (404),
while the GitHub release is tagged `v3.97.4`. The customManager therefore strips the `v` with
extractVersionTemplate, exactly as the gitleaks and glitchtip_cli managers do, and the value
written here is what goes after the colon.
⚠️ NO `trufflehog_sha256`, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT. The other four
scanners are downloaded as release assets and `sha256sum -c`'d, so a digest beside the version is
a check something actually runs. Here the only two inputs the action exposes are `image` and
`version`, joined with a colon — `image@sha256:...` cannot be expressed through them, so a digest
written here would be a pin NOTHING VERIFIES, which this repository treats as worse than no pin.
What is recorded instead is the measurement: on 2026-09-06 the tag `3.97.4` and the tag `latest`
resolved to the SAME manifest, sha256:562bc231afa9de3d04de44cfe624252b08207de1fc3cebc5e7ed92bed7f279e4,
so pinning the version changes nothing today and freezes it from tomorrow. ⬜ The residual is
stated and not dressed as coverage: a registry tag is mutable, and nothing in this repository
would see it move. Closing that needs the action to accept a digest, or this lane to stop using
the wrapper and run the container itself.
$store_publishing_comment: THE TWO STORE-SUBMISSION TOOLCHAINS, ADDED 2026-09-07 ([ADR 067] decision 8, phase 3 unit store-lanes).
They landed as EXACT pins written inside the code that runs them and nowhere else, which is the
[pipeline 14]O-9 hole this file exists to close: tooling/ci/assert-update-coverage.mjs quantifies over
the keys HERE, so both were outside its domain and its EXIT 0 said nothing about either. The unit's own
acceptance recorded that green as if it had covered them; it had not.
BOTH ARE NOW READ FROM THIS FILE AT RUN TIME rather than restated beside it. That is deliberate and it
is the opposite of the gitleaks decision two blocks up: there, scan-secrets.mjs's VALIDATED_AGAINST must
stay a literal precisely BECAUSE it is compared against the installed version, and reading the pin would
make that comparison compare a value with itself. Nothing here compares anything: the pin is simply the
version to install, so a second copy would be a copy that can only drift.
web_ext  — the AMO signer. extensions/scripts/publish-amo.mjs runs `npx --yes web-ext@<pin> sign`.
EXACT and not a range: v10 changed what `sign` DOES (it signs and submits a listed version
rather than only signing), which is the whole reason the AMO lane can make a first submission.
⚠ THREE SPELLINGS OF web-ext EXIST AND ONLY THIS ONE IS THE SIGNER. extensions.yml:612 lints
with the RANGE `web-ext@8` and :1976 with the exact 8.10.0; both are the CI lint lane, outside
the store-lanes region, and are named as a residue rather than edited. A v8 lint is not evidence
about a v10 sign.
msstore_cli — the Microsoft Store submission transport. .github/workflows/submit-windows-store.yml installs
it with winget (`--id Microsoft.MSStoreCLI --version <pin>`) and tooling/release/submit-windows-store.mjs
drives it. Renovate resolves it from the GitHub releases of microsoft/msstore-cli, whose tags carry
a leading `v` (checked 2026-09-07: the latest release tag is `v0.4.2`, name `Microsoft Store CLI
v0.4.2`), so its customManager strips that prefix and this value never carries one.
$updateExemptions_comment: [pipeline 14]O-9 — EVERY KEY ABOVE MUST BE REACHED BY AN UPDATE MECHANISM, OR APPEAR HERE WITH A
WRITTEN REASON. tooling/ci/assert-update-coverage.mjs enforces both directions: an unreached pin
with no exemption fails, and an exemption for a pin that no longer exists fails too, so a waiver
cannot outlive the thing it waived.
THE WAIVER LIVES IN THIS FILE, BESIDE THE PIN, DELIBERATELY. A list of excuses in another file is
one that goes stale silently, because the diff that removes a pin never shows it.
🔴 WHY THE GUARD RUNS THE MATCHERS INSTEAD OF READING THE CONFIG. All five customManagers in
renovate.json were once written with a REGEX where a GLOB was expected. They matched nothing and
proposed no update for any toolchain pin for weeks — while 'an update-mechanism configuration
exists and is enabled', the drafted acceptance, reported green the entire time. Only applying the
pattern to a real path, and the matchString to the real content, can see that.
🔬 `wrangler` was UNCOVERED until 2026-08-02 and was found by that guard's first run: the tool
that publishes production, declared here and advanced by nobody. It now has a customManager.
